dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Brainstorm conclusion plus the 2026-10-07 incident: entering the feat/fleet-dashboard bay without running a leg needed /wt, a non-Waybill skill, because only a named /waybill:next moves a session and it always runs the leg.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Goals state observable output: an ENTER BAY: line in bay --markdown for any bay the operator is not already inside, a cleanup warning in WARNINGS, and bay.md acting on the line with exit-first semantics.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Operator chose named node tests per behavior plus one live smoke judgment covering EnterWorktree, the bay-to-bay exit, and /clear persistence.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Operator approved the IN/OUT strawman as listed, single phase, no Full/Stretch tiers.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The one divergence from next (entering a bay whose next leg is cleanup) was decided explicitly and is surfaced as a warning; sequencing against feat/next-drives-the-route decided as independent.

problem: No Waybill command moves a session into a docket's bay without also running a leg there. `/waybill:bay <branch>` cuts or finds the bay and prints a waybill but never moves the session; the only mover is `/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>`, whose `ENTER BAY:` line is always followed by a `RUN:` that starts the leg.

The operator hits this whenever they want to stand in a bay to look around, finish by hand, or check state mid-session — on 2026-10-07 entering `feat/fleet-dashboard` took `/wt`, a personal skill outside Waybill that knows nothing about dockets. The gap widens once `feat/next-drives-the-route` lands and a named `next` always executes.
goals: `waybill bay --markdown <branch>` prints `ENTER BAY: <bay path>` whenever the operator is not already inside that bay — newly cut or pre-existing — and never prints `RUN:` or `NEXT LEG:`.
When the bay's next leg is `cleanup`, `bay` still enters and its output carries a WARNINGS entry saying cleanup will remove the bay.
`/waybill:bay` moves the session into the bay with EnterWorktree, leaving any other worktree first with ExitWorktree (keep), falls back to a `cd <path>` line when the move fails, and then stops.
Every prose surface that says `bay` does not move the session is brought in line.

successCriteria.criterion: bay --markdown prints ENTER BAY: for a newly cut and a pre-existing bay, with no RUN: or NEXT LEG: line

check.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-name-pattern 'bay markdown enters the bay' tests/cli.test.js 2>&1) && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'

successCriteria.criterion: bay --markdown prints no ENTER BAY: for a bay the operator is already inside (the test asserts its cwd is the bay path)

check.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-name-pattern 'bay markdown does not enter a bay it is already inside' tests/cli.test.js 2>&1) && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'

successCriteria.criterion: A bay whose next leg is cleanup is still entered, and both terminal and markdown output carry the cleanup warning

check.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-name-pattern 'bay warns when the next leg is cleanup' tests/cli.test.js 2>&1) && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'

successCriteria.criterion: commands/bay.md allows EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree, carries the ENTER BAY: and exit-first rules, and its menu descriptions promise entry

check.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-name-pattern 'bay.md enters the bay' tests/commands.test.js 2>&1) && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'

successCriteria.criterion: The guide's waybill samples still match the re-blessed goldens after the booking body changes

check.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-name-pattern 'samples match their goldens' tests/guide.test.js 2>&1) && printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qE '^# pass [1-9]'

successCriteria.criterion: The stale 'bay does not move you' prose is gone from bay.md, the bay booking and its guide copy, and bay.md names ExitWorktree

check.cmd: ! grep -qF 'once I have typed' commands/bay.md && ! grep -qF 'prints its waybill' commands/bay.md && ! grep -qF 'moves the next session into the bay' bookings/waybill-bay.md docs/guide/01-ride-along.md && grep -q 'ExitWorktree' commands/bay.md

check.judgment: The PR's CI run of `node --test tests/` is green (the suite runs ~210s, past the verify timeout).

successCriteria.criterion: A live session lands and stays in the bay

check.judgment: Operator runs `/waybill:bay <existing branch>` from the trunk and again from inside another bay, confirms the session is in the target bay each time, then types /clear and confirms it is still there.

mvp.item: CLI: `bay --markdown` passes `{ bay, enter: true }` unless already inside, so the renderer prints `ENTER BAY: <path>` with no token (no RUN:/NEXT LEG:). The heading stays first, as the command-surface spec requires, so `ENTER BAY:` follows it
mvp.reason: The CLI decides when to move, as it does for next; the renderer line already exists (src/waybill.js:364-369). bay.md's rules for it are new, adapted from next.md:71-90.

mvp.item: CLI: when `state.leg === 'cleanup'`, push a warning onto `state.warnings` so it renders in WARNINGS in both terminal and markdown output
mvp.reason: Operator chose to enter cleanup bays, with a warning; state.warnings is the existing path (onRamp, cli.js:436-457).

mvp.item: commands/bay.md: on a line beginning `ENTER BAY:` (wherever it appears in the block), always call ExitWorktree (keep) first — treating "no active worktree session" as fine to continue — then EnterWorktree with the path; on an EnterWorktree failure say why in one line, show `cd <path>` and the block, and stop
mvp.reason: The move itself. bay.md cannot tell whether it is in another worktree (no git on its allowed-tools), so the exit is unconditional; that is /mar's approach, and ExitWorktree is a no-op outside a worktree session.

mvp.item: commands/bay.md: allowed-tools gains EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree and ToolSearch
mvp.reason: The allowed-tools list is restrictive; an undeclared tool is silently unavailable. Both worktree tools were deferred in this session and needed ToolSearch to load (as /mar's test pins); the live smoke confirms.

mvp.item: No-arg menu descriptions: `no bay yet — cuts one and enters it`, `new branch — cuts it and its bay, and enters it`, `bay exists — enters it`
mvp.reason: The menu promises what the choice does.

mvp.item: Prose sweep: bookings/waybill-bay.md (with tests/golden/bay.md, bay.txt and the docs/guide/01-ride-along.md sample), README.md bay sections, docs/guide/01-ride-along.md and 03-reference.md, src/help.js walkthrough steps 3 and 5 (with tests/golden/help.txt), the src/cli.js:145 and bay() comments, commands/bay.md comment blocks
mvp.reason: Learning from next-from-anywhere: behavior prose outside src/ goes stale unless every hit is listed.

mvp.item: Tests: re-bless the bay-cut, bay and help goldens, replace the 'bay already exists' starts-with assertion, add the named tests above, update the bay.md allowed-tools assertion (tests/commands.test.js:471)
mvp.reason: Every functional change is pinned by a test that fails first.

outOfScope.reason: That is next's job; bay enters, shows the waybill, and stops.

decisions.reason: Entering is what the operator wants whenever they name a branch.

decisions.decision: Enter a bay whose next leg is cleanup, with a warning
decisions.reason: Naming the branch is a deliberate request to go in; cleanup runs by branch name from anywhere.

decisions.decision: From inside another bay, ExitWorktree (keep) then EnterWorktree
decisions.reason: Bay-to-bay is the commonest reason for the feature; /wt already proves exit-first works.
/wt is outside Waybill and knows nothing about dockets or the waybill.

decisions.decision: Cleanup warning via state.warnings in the WARNINGS block
decisions.rejected: A dedicated line beside ENTER BAY:
decisions.reason: Reuses the existing renderer path in both outputs; no new literal for bay.md to key on.

decisions.decision: Verify with named node tests plus one live smoke judgment
decisions.reason: EnterWorktree and /clear persistence are session behavior no node test can execute.

decisions.rejected: Block on it, or land first by plan
decisions.reason: This change touches bay only; whichever merges second rebases and re-blesses goldens.

decisions.decision: bay.md always calls ExitWorktree (keep) before EnterWorktree, continuing past "no active worktree session"
decisions.rejected: Exit only when inside another worktree (detected via git rev-parse, as /wt does)
decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic: bay.md has no git on its allowed-tools and the CLI emits no such signal; an unconditional exit needs neither.

decisions.decision: Keep bay's heading first; bay.md keys on an `ENTER BAY:` line wherever it appears
decisions.rejected: Move ENTER BAY: above the heading, as next prints it
decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic: the command-surface spec requires the heading first; keying by line start needs no spec change.

decisions.decision: Each test criterion gates on node --test's own exit code plus a pass-count grep
decisions.rejected: Grep for '# pass' alone, with one criterion re-running its file to check '# fail'
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: a pattern matching several tests let one pass mask a failure, and the double run doubled time against the verify cap.

decisions.decision: Add a negated-grep criterion on today's stale bay prose, with an ExitWorktree positive twin
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: goal 4 had no criterion, so a sweep that missed a surface would still pass.
